# property-testing-openapi

Namespace: `Rasuvaeff\PropertyTesting\OpenApi`.

Purpose: create reproducible, JSON-compatible OpenAPI request cases and turn
them into PSR-7 requests before an explicit transport is called.

Public API:
- `RequestCaseArbitrary::forOperation(Operation): ArbitraryInterface`
  (`SchemaArbitraryCompiler` behind it is `@internal`). Parameters: OAS 3.0
  `nullable` and `null` enum members dropped (null = absent branch); path
  strings non-empty and free of `/`/`\` at every nesting level, unsafe enum
  members dropped, `uri`/`uri-reference`/`url` path formats fail closed.
  Bodies: request direction of the schema (`readOnly` dropped from
  `properties`/`required`, nested and inside combinators).
- Compile-time fail-closed (`UnsupportedGeneration`) on: `pattern` +
  asserted `format`; a length window outside the format's band (uuid 36,
  date 10, date-time 29, ipv4 7–15, email 6–36, uri/url 12–55); `uniqueItems`
  over a finite item domain (`boolean`, `enum`, `const`, `null`) smaller than
  `minItems`; `not.type` covering every declared type; an `allOf` branch
  bounding `additionalProperties` that does not declare every sibling
  property. Fractional integer bounds round inward; an open number bound
  steps inside by min(0.1, window/4).
- `RequestMaterializer::materialize(Operation, array $case): RequestInterface`
  builds the request target against the operation's first effective server
  (relative server -> path-only URI, absolute server -> absolute URI);
  `withBaseUri(string)` replaces the declared server with
  `scheme://host[:port][/base]` or a root-relative `/base` (no trailing slash,
  userinfo, query, or fragment; `InvalidArgumentException` otherwise). An
  absolute override that contradicts every declared server fails contract
  validation with `request.server.mismatch`.
- `TransportInterface::send(RequestInterface): ResponseInterface`
- `CallableTransport` and `Psr15Transport` execute an explicit transport boundary;
  `Psr15Transport($handler, $serverRequests, afterRequest: callable,
  ?StreamFactoryInterface $streams, ?UploadedFileFactoryInterface
  $uploadedFiles)` runs the optional reset hook once in `finally`, including
  when the handler throws, and populates the server request like the SAPI:
  `queryParams` (URI), `cookieParams` (`Cookie`), `parsedBody` for
  form-urlencoded and multipart (`parse_str()` name semantics), and
  `uploadedFiles` for multipart parts with a filename when both factories are
  given (otherwise file parts are dropped). The body stream is passed through
  rewound. The materializer emits `filename="<part>"` for binary parts.
- Security: requests target the document's `servers` (or `baseUri()`); do not
  run untrusted contracts through a networked transport.
- `SecurityRequirement`, `CredentialsProviderInterface`, `CredentialsUnavailable`,
  and `SecuritySelector` (`@internal`; reached through
  `ContractSuite::credentials()`) model OR alternatives and AND schemes
  without putting secrets in generated cases; an empty requirement object
  selects anonymous credentials without calling the provider.
- `Credentials` accepts string or list<string> values, normalizes its public
  headers/query/cookies maps to list<string>, and applies them at materialization
  time; pass the selected credentials as the optional third argument to
  `RequestMaterializer::materialize`.
- `NegativeRequestCaseArbitrary::forOperation(Operation)` removes one required
  request component and records `misuse.kind = 'missing-required'`.
- `NegativeRequestCaseArbitrary::typeMismatchForOperation(Operation)` replaces
  one required scalar integer/number/boolean/null parameter with an invalid wire
  value and records `misuse.kind = 'type'`; both methods throw
  `UnsupportedGeneration` when their mutation cannot be constructed.
- `NegativeRequestCaseArbitrary::enumMismatchForOperation(Operation)` replaces
  one required scalar enum parameter with a value outside the enum and records
  `misuse.kind = 'enum'`.
- `NegativeRequestCaseArbitrary::constMismatchForOperation(Operation)` replaces
  one required scalar `const` parameter with a different value and records
  `misuse.kind = 'const'`.
- `NegativeRequestCaseArbitrary::boundaryMismatchForOperation(Operation)`
  replaces one required integer/number parameter with a wire value just outside
  its `minimum`/`maximum` bound (boolean exclusive bounds honoured) and records
  `misuse.kind = 'boundary'`.
- `NegativeRequestCaseArbitrary::lengthMismatchForOperation(Operation)`
  replaces one required string parameter with a value just outside its
  `minLength`/`maxLength` bound and records `misuse.kind = 'length'`;
  parameters with `enum`/`const`/`pattern`/`format` are skipped.
- `NegativeRequestCaseArbitrary::formatMismatchForOperation(Operation)`
  replaces one required string parameter with a fixed witness violating its
  `format` (uuid, email, ipv4, uri, uri-reference, date, date-time) and records
  `misuse.kind = 'format'`; `url` is not asserted by the backend and is skipped.
- `NegativeRequestCaseArbitrary::patternMismatchForOperation(Operation)`
  replaces one required string parameter with a searched value failing its
  `pattern` (the pattern is the `preg_match()` oracle; bounded alphabet samples
  and mutations of an accepted value) and records `misuse.kind = 'pattern'`;
  parameters with `enum`/`const`/`format` are skipped and an exhausted search
  budget or a PCRE error fails closed.
- `NegativeRequestCaseArbitrary::additionalPropertyForOperation(Operation)`
  adds one undeclared property to a required JSON object body with
  `additionalProperties: false` and records
  `misuse.kind = 'additional-properties'`.
- `NegativeRequestCaseArbitrary::mediaTypeMismatchForOperation(Operation)`
  keeps the valid JSON body but sends it under an undeclared Content-Type and
  records `misuse.kind = 'media-type'`; wildcard media types fail closed.
- `NegativeRequestCaseArbitrary::malformedJsonForOperation(Operation)` replaces
  the required JSON body with a raw malformed payload (`encoding: 'raw'`) and
  records `misuse.kind = 'json-syntax'`.
- `UnsupportedGeneration` for unsupported schema/body/parameter input.
- `ContractSuite::fromContract(Contract, RequestFactoryInterface, StreamFactoryInterface)`
  builds the framework-neutral suite model. Fluent configuration:
  `operations(list)` (explicit allow-list, unknown keys throw),
  `allSafeOperations()` (opt-in for GET/HEAD), `exclude(list)`,
  `allowUnsafeOperations()` (required for unsafe methods; without it
  `operationKeys()` throws `SuiteConfigurationError`),
  `transport(TransportInterface)`, `credentials(CredentialsProviderInterface)`,
  `rejectionPolicy(RejectionPolicy)`, `baseUri(string)` (materialize against
  an explicit base URI instead of the declared server).
- `ContractSuite::operationKeys(): list<string>` resolves the selection.
- `ContractSuite::exampleCases(string $operationKey): array<string, CaseData>`
  (via the `@internal` `DocumentExamples::forOperation(Operation)`) derives named valid cases
  from the document's `example`/`examples`: parameter/media-type `examples`
  map (Example Objects with `value`) -> named cases, one per distinct name
  across all parts; `example`, then Schema Object `example`, then
  `examples[0]` -> the unnamed case `example`. Missing parts fall back to the
  unnamed example, then to a fixed-seed base case. Deterministic under every
  seed; `externalValue`-only entries and multipart bodies contribute nothing;
  body examples lose their `readOnly` members; unrepresentable parameter
  examples throw `UnsupportedGeneration`. Not
  validated here: an invalid example fails `checkValid()` before transport.
- `ContractSuite::validCases(string $operationKey)` /
  `negativeCases(string $operationKey)` return case arbitraries for a selected
  operation; `negativeCases` weights every constructively supported negative
  category and throws `UnsupportedGeneration` when none applies.
- `CheckFailed` (thrown by the checks below) exposes `?ValidationResult $result`
  for validation failures; its message renders every violation through
  `ValidationResultFormatter` (operation, code, location, instancePath,
  specPointer, bounded expected/actual, sensitive actual values redacted).
- `ContractSuite::checkValid(string $operationKey, array $case)` validates the
  materialized request before transport, sends it, and throws `CheckFailed` on
  a 5xx status or a non-conforming exchange. Declared non-JSON responses are
  opaque (no schema) or validated as a string (string-typed schema) by
  `openapi-contract` ^0.2.1; only `response.body.unsupported` remains.
- `ContractSuite::checkNegative(string $operationKey, array $case)` requires
  `misuse` metadata and pre-transport invalidity, then throws `CheckFailed`
  if invalid input produces a 5xx or, with a configured `RejectionPolicy`,
  a status outside the accepted selectors.
- `RejectionPolicy::rejectWith(int|string ...)` builds the opt-in negative
  oracle from exact status codes or `NXX` ranges;
  `forOperation(string $operationKey, ...)` overrides selectors per operation;
  `accepts(string $operationKey, int $status): bool`.
- `ContractSuite::reproduce(string $operationKey, array $case, RedactionPolicy)`
  renders a redacted curl command; credentials are never applied there.
- `RequestReproducer::curl(Operation, array $case, RedactionPolicy)` is the
  `@internal` standalone form; `RedactionPolicy(headers, queryParameters, cookies,
  bodyPaths)` names extra redactions on top of the default header set
  (Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie). Body previews are
  byte-bounded and UTF-8 safe.
- `SuiteConfigurationError` for selection/transport misconfiguration;
  `CheckFailed` for built-in check failures.
- `ResponseCaseArbitrary::forOperation(Operation, int $status): ArbitraryInterface`
  generates valid, corpus-safe response cases `{operationKey, status, headers,
  body: null|{mediaType, encoding: 'json'|'raw', value}, misuse: null}` for the
  Response Object the status resolves to (exact -> NXX -> default via
  `Operation::responseFor`); required headers always present, `writeOnly`
  properties left out; `jsonBody(Operation, int)` exposes the response-direction
  media type + schema. Undeclared status / required header without schema /
  non-JSON content throw `UnsupportedGeneration`.
- `ResponseMaterializer(ResponseFactoryInterface, StreamFactoryInterface)
  ::materialize(Operation, array $case): ResponseInterface` builds the PSR-7
  response (headers serialized with the `simple` style: percent-encoded, lists
  joined with commas; JSON body is schema-aware, so `{}` stays an object;
  `Content-Type` from the case).
- `NegativeResponseCaseArbitrary::forOperation(Operation, int $status)` is the
  weighted union of constructive invalid-response categories; per-category
  methods `undeclaredStatusForOperation`, `missingRequiredHeaderForOperation`,
  `missingRequiredForOperation`, `typeMismatchForOperation`,
  `enumMismatchForOperation`, `constMismatchForOperation`,
  `boundaryMismatchForOperation`, `lengthMismatchForOperation`,
  `patternMismatchForOperation`, `additionalPropertyForOperation`,
  `mediaTypeMismatchForOperation`, `malformedJsonForOperation`. Body targets
  are top-level object properties or the scalar/array root (`misuse.name` =
  `$`); every case is provably invalid under `Contract::validateResponse()`,
  misuse survives shrinking, unconstructible categories throw
  `UnsupportedGeneration`.
- `OperationProperty::check(ContractSuite, string $operationKey, int $runs = 100, ?int $seed = null)`
  runs `exampleCases()` first (before corpus replay and the random phase,
  under every seed); a failing example throws `OperationPropertyFailed` with
  `$example` set to its name, the case unshrunk and `runsBeforeFailure = 0`.
  runs the valid phase always and the negative phase when the operation has a
  constructible misuse category; a falsified phase throws
  `OperationPropertyFailed` (operation key, phase, `CounterExample`, redacted
  curl reproducer). `PROPERTY_RUNS` overrides runs, `PROPERTY_SEED` fixes the
  seed (an explicit `seed:` wins and disables corpus replay), `PROPERTY_DB`
  names a directory corpus or `redis://host[:port][/key-prefix]` shared corpus;
  Redis uses ext-redis or predis and connects lazily.
- `OpenApiOperations::keys(ContractSuite): iterable<string, array{string}>`
  yields the resolved selection as named single-argument tuples for Testo
  `#[DataProvider]` and PHPUnit `#[DataProviderExternal]` providers.
- `OperationCoverage` is a caller-owned, process-local record attached with
  `ContractSuite::coverage(OperationCoverage)`; every `checkValid()`/
  `checkNegative()` trial records `(operationKey, response status)` after
  transport (a 5xx counts). Hold one instance per run (static property) —
  suites rebuilt per test case and suites derived by fluent calls share it.
  `record(string, int)`, `exercised(): list<string>`,
  `report(list<string> $selected): CoverageReport`.
- `ContractSuite::coverageReport(): CoverageReport` restricts the record to
  `operationKeys()`; throws `SuiteConfigurationError` without a record.
- `CoverageReport` (readonly): `selected`, `covered`, `uncovered` (selection
  order), `statuses: array<string, array<int, positive-int>>` (sorted, only
  selected operations), `isComplete()`, `assertComplete()` (opt-in gate,
  throws `CoverageIncomplete` with `$report`), `toArray()`, `toJson()`
  (stable, `statuses` always a JSON object). Statuses are diagnostics, not a
  gate. Merge per-process reports outside the package.

`RequestCaseData` has `operationKey`, separate path/query/headers/cookies maps,
an optional JSON-compatible body: `{mediaType, encoding: 'json'|'raw'|'form', value}`
or `{mediaType, encoding: 'multipart', boundary, parts}` (binary parts use base64), and
`misuse: null`; `encoding: 'raw'` appears only in malformed-JSON negative cases.
It must contain only JSON-compatible values and never secrets or PSR-7 objects.
Multipart parts are scalar/binary only (nested objects/arrays throw
`UnsupportedGeneration`); the part content type is the OAS default of the item
schema unless the Encoding Object names one. An empty array/object parameter or
form property is omitted at materialization (RFC 6570: undefined), and required
array/object parameters and form properties are generated non-empty.
Required parameters and request bodies are always generated. Optional parameters
and JSON bodies are generated as both present and absent branches.
Object generation supports bounded `minProperties`, `maxProperties`, and
boolean or schema-valued `additionalProperties`.
The constructive `not` subset supports `const`, `enum`, and `type` exclusions;
other negative assertions fail closed.
